solver_notes: Native pthread/C11 regression model on physical aarch64, not a claimed upstream CPython patch and not an execution of upstream CPython. The metadata repo is inconsistent (torvalds/linux with CPython Python/pylifecycle.c), so the harness isolates the required interpreter-list and tstate lifetime protocol. Legacy ordering unlinks and unmaps a page-backed tstate before the daemon PyEval_SaveThread-equivalent read, producing deterministic SIGSEGV (shell exit 139; Python returncode -11). Fixed teardown acquires head_mutex around every interpreter-list check/unlink and tstate acquisition, holds a temporary atomic reference across the GIL-release section, and uses atomic acq_rel decrements for final destruction. Real concurrent stress executed 128 deletion rounds x 8 daemon savers with 53,755 successful saves and 54,108 mutex acquisitions. An initial ASan build could not start on this aarch64 runtime: sanitizer_allocator_primary64.h CHECK failed on its reserved address range before test execution. No result is inferred from that environment failure; the deterministic mmap/munmap negative control and normal pthread fixed stress were used instead. An initial compile error (sizeof before declaration) was corrected before any passing result. file_sha256_of_this_json is computed with that field set to the empty string; solution_payload_sha256.txt binds final transmitted bytes.
